messages:
Mia (Design): dropped a compact mock for the version history timeline. Key idea: collapse long timelines into a single-line scrubber with focusable markers for events (deploy, canary, promote, rollback). Thoughts? :mag:
Jordan (PM): nice. Two quick questions: 1) how do users discover the markers on hover-only devices? 2) what are we calling the primary action on markers? 'Promote' or 'Advance'?
Mia (Design): good Qs. For discovery we show a faint dot row and animate the active marker on hover/focus. For mobile we allow tap-to-expand. For the action label I'm leaning to 'Promote' because it aligns with our rollout copy elsewhere.
Sam (Eng): from a11y and implementation POV, hover-only cues are bad. Make every marker keyboard-focusable and provide a visible focus ring. We should avoid complex SVGs per marker to keep CPU down when there are hundreds of events.
Anya (Accessibility): +1 on focusable controls. Also microcopy: avoid words like 'promote' without context. Screen reader users need the target version in the announcement. Suggested SR text: 'Event: canary started at five percent, promoted to 50 percent on 2025-06-01 14:02 by @lee'.
Mia (Design): noted. I'll add an aria-label for each marker with that full sentence. Visually we'll keep the short verb 'Promote'.
Devon (QA): from testing perspective, please expose a data-test-id on each interactive marker and the expanded panel so we can automate e2e checks for focus, keyboard nav, and the diffs link.
Sam (Eng): will do. Also consider limiting live updates frequency; the timeline can get noisy for busy projects. We can batch UI updates every 2s and still feel real-time.
Jordan (PM): copy debate: the timeline shows a 'Pause rollout' affordance when a canary is running. Some PMs prefer 'Pause' vs 'Halt'. Which is clearer?
Anya (Accessibility): 'Pause' is more conversational. 'Halt' sounds abrupt and could alarm screen reader users. Also ensure the button has aria-pressed state when active and an accessible name like: 'Pause rollout for service X. Currently running at 5 percent.'
Mia (Design): OK 'Pause rollout' it is. We'll include aria-pressed and tooltip content that reads on focus. Tooltip should not be the only accessible text.
Jordan (PM): what about contrast on the timeline markers? design mock uses a pale blue for canary, which fails WCAG 4.5:1 small text. We need contrast >= 3:1 for non-text UI components.
Mia (Design): I can bump saturation or add a dark stroke around markers. Which is preferred?
Anya (Accessibility): prefer a higher contrast fill and keep stroke optional. Also add a visible focus ring in a WCAG-compliant color. For colorblind users, use distinct shapes/icons as well, not color alone.
Sam (Eng): performance/implementation note: use CSS shape rendering and a single sprite sheet for icons. Avoid adding extra DOM per marker; render markers via canvas layer when event count > 200 and overlay an accessible layer for keyboard targets. That keeps perf good and still keyboard navigable.
Devon (QA): one more: timeline scrubber animation was flickering in the prototype when many updates came in. Recommend reducing animation duration to 120ms and debouncing keyframe restarts.
Mia (Design): good catch, I will update animation to be minimal and only run on active focus/hover to reduce motion. Also will add an accessible setting: 'Reduce motion in timeline' that respects OS-level prefers-reduced-motion.
Jordan (PM): final UX ask: clarify the confirmation flow when a user hits 'Revert' from a marker. The modal should show who triggered the original change, the diff link, and the exact version ID. Devon, can QA own the regression tests for that modal?
Devon (QA): yes. We'll test keyboard-only confirm, focus trap, SR announcements, and the double-confirm safety mode for orgs that enable it.
Mia (Design): action list: 1) make markers keyboard-focusable with clear focus ring, 2) supply full aria-labels per event, 3) increase marker contrast and shape variety, 4) add data-test-ids, 5) optimize rendering for >200 events, 6) tune animations and respect reduced-motion. I'll push updated frames by EOD.
deploy-bot: Notice: canary rollout started for service Payments v4.1 at 1745001234 by @lee  target 5% window 15m.
Jordan (PM): perfect. We'll review the updated mock in tomorrow's design crit. Thanks all!
